# 1. Introduction

# 2. Methods

Follow the approaches and reporting conventions used in the module and required in the CA Phase 2 rubric.

-   Provide a concise methodology overview.
-   State your cut-off value (typically p \< .05 unless otherwise specified).

## 2.1 Univariate Exploration

-   Describe how you examined each variable:

    -   Heuristic normality assessment of continuous variables to derive appropriate summary statistics

    -   Frequencies / proportions for the binary outcome

    -   Visuals appropriate for each type (histograms, barplots, density curves)
    
    - Missingness checks

      - Patterns of missing data

      - Decisions regarding exclusion or imputation (if relevant)

    - Notes on variable suitability

      - Any issues identified that may require transformation


## 2.2 Bivariate Exploration

-   Describe how you justified predictor inclusion:

    -   Visuals

        -   Boxplots for continuous × binary outcome

        -   Barplots for categorical × binary outcome

    -   Correlation-type tests (Pearson/Spearman/Kendall chi-square, etc., as appropriate)

    -   Group difference tests (t-tests, non-parametric alternatives)

-   Describe any patterns suggesting predictor relevance. If there are none you can still include them as control.

# 3. Data Preparation and Exploration Results

Follow the approaches and reporting conventions used in the module and required in the CA Phase 2 rubric.

-   Present your univariate and bivariate analysis.

- Describe preliminary patterns, direction and strength of relationships, differences, identification of any potential nonlinear relationships


Note: predictors can be included even if the relationship appears weak, especially as control variables. Theoretical justification is acceptable when exploratory patterns are weak.
